title: Don’t Just Keep Coming Home. Learn to Live There.
headline: What Does It Mean to Abide in Christ?
headline_sub: Don’t Just Keep Coming Home. Learn to Live There.
tagline: The goal isn’t to become excellent at repeatedly visiting Jesus. The goal is to learn to live with Him.
seo_title: What Does "Abide in Christ" Mean? John 15:4-5 for Men | TheWrkShop
seo_description: Return and remain are not the same thing. A devotional for men on John 15:4-9: Jesus never said visit Me when necessary; He said remain.
verse_text: Remain in me, as I also remain in you…. Neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in me.

scriptures.text: Remain in me, as I also remain in you…. Neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in me.
As the Father has loved me, so have I loved you. Now remain in my love.

items: All week we have been learning one word: return.
Fear? Return.
Temptation? Return.
Failure? Return.
Success? Return.

blocks.text: But underneath the whole week is a deeper question:

items: If we’re not careful, we can build an entire Christian life around wandering and returning.
But Jesus offers something greater than repeatedly visiting Him after we’ve wandered.
He says, “Remain in Me.”
Maybe the goal isn’t merely becoming better at coming home.
Maybe the goal is learning to live there.

sections.label: Return and Remain Are Not the Same Thing

items: Return says, “I wandered.”
Remain says, “This is where I live.”
Return restores orientation.
Remain cultivates formation.
We will need return many times.
But Jesus’ invitation is bigger: remain.
Sunday? Visit Jesus.
Morning devotional? Visit Jesus.
Emergency? Visit Jesus.
Then return to “normal life.”
But Jesus doesn’t say, “Visit Me when necessary.”
He says remain. Stay. Abide. Make your home here.
Jesus isn’t asking to become one more part of your life.
He is inviting you to live your life in Him.

sections.label: Abiding Isn’t Thinking About Jesus Every Second

items: You have work to do, children to raise, problems to solve.
A faithful husband doesn’t consciously think about his wife during every second of every meeting.
But he remains married during the meeting.
That covenant keeps governing his identity, boundaries and decisions.
Abiding is continuing life under Christ’s relational lordship.
You aren’t merely learning to think about Jesus.
You are learning to live with Jesus.
Thought captivity is not the center of Christianity. Christ is.
The best time to prepare for the thought is before the thought arrives.
Familiarity with truth shortens the distance to return.
